findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\scene-lowOrbit.png (Central Pacific circle, x 445-560, y 430-560); same view in lowOrbit-node.png and hover-add-maneuver.png; accept-occlusion.png (Central Atlantic ellipse at x 770-803, y 380-450: notch plus overshooting spur at the top tip, dimmed stretch at the bottom tip; gap in the Central Pacific circle next to the pad icon); synthetic-earth.png (zone on the dark limb is a broken green blob)
findings.defect: Recovery-zone circles are solid lines lying on the body, but toward the limb they break up into irregular dashes: in scene-lowOrbit.png the Central Pacific circle has five separate gaps (top-left, three on the inner right side, one at the bottom hook) and a stray tick; at the tips of the Central Atlantic ellipse there is a 1 px notch with a spur. It reads as z-fighting between the line and the planet surface. The breakup starts about 64 degrees from the sub-camera point (outer ~10 % of the disc radius) and gets worse to the limb.
findings.realReference: A circle drawn on a globe is one continuous stroke right up to the limb, where it simply foreshortens into the edge and disappears behind it (KSP/Orbiter ground markers, any GIS globe). No gaps at vertices or mid-chord.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/scene.ts addZoneLine (lines 1057-1066) sets occlusionSlack to the RADIAL depth of the deepest chord midpoint below the sphere (+1e-3 R). src/map/gpu/shaders.ts occlusion() (line 45: `tp <= t1 + tol + slack`) applies that slack as a distance ALONG THE VIEW RAY past the near intersection. A point at radial depth s under the surface, seen at incidence angle phi, lies s / cos(phi) along the ray inside the sphere, which is unbounded at the limb, so mid-chord fragments are judged hidden while fragments at the vertices survive. The 0.9 px faint tolerance (scene.ts:725, constants.ts FAINT_CHORD_TOLERANCE_PX) gives only ~23 chords for a 95 px circle, so the chord sag is ~10 km.
findings.fixDirection: Make the slack radial: for lines that carry a slack, test against a sphere of radius R - slack (t1 from R - slack; not occluded when dperp >= R - slack) instead of adding slack to the ray distance; mirror it in src/map/occlusion.ts if zone outlines are ever tested on the CPU. Also bound the 3-D chord sag of zone circles (maximum turn per segment, or sample them at the patch tolerance: they are 2 px wide at 0.9 alpha, not faint), or lift the vertices to R / cos(halfStep) so chords never dip under the sphere. Add a browser spec with a zone centred 75-88 degrees from the sub-camera point that walks the projected circle and asserts no gap pixels on the visible side.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\lowOrbit-node.png (gizmo at x 740-840, y 175-270, label at x 828-962, y 209-238)
findings.defect: The gizmo of the SELECTED node is drawn at 35 % alpha because the node sits just behind the Earth's limb: the handles are dark purple / olive / teal on black (normal handle peaks at RGB 80,33,88 against 207,84,223 when not dimmed; contrast to the background about 1.7:1), the node label 'Node 1 dv 426.1 m/s' is grey (peak 82,86,90). The element the player is editing looks disabled, and its axis lines are drawn across the planet disc. This is the package's hero screenshot of gizmo plus panel. The hand-off lists it as a known limit (alpha floor 0.35), but it is plainly visible.
findings.realReference: In KSP and in every DCC manipulator the active gizmo is always drawn on top at full brightness; that the node itself is behind the body is shown on the node icon only (hollow or dashed ring), never by dimming the handles the player must grab.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/controller.ts line 820: `const a = Math.max(0.35, 1 - n.hidden)` is used for the node icon, all six handles, their axis bars (0.55 * a, line 833) and the label (line 842), selected or not.
findings.fixDirection: For the selected node use alpha 1 for handles, bars and label regardless of n.hidden; signal occlusion on the node icon alone (hollow / dashed ring variant of ICON.node). Keep the 0.35 floor only for unselected nodes. Add a pixel assertion in the lowOrbit node spec that a handle of a selected, occluded node reaches its full colour.

findings.defect: In the top-down view of the orbit (the default way to look at it) the normal and antinormal handles sit exactly ON the radial axis: both magenta triangles are threaded by the cyan radial bar and the magenta normal bar is drawn collinear on top of it (purple-cyan mixed line). Four handles and two bars share one screen line within 22-58 px of the node, so normal cannot be told from radial and the nearer normal triangles steal the pick. In accept-panel.png the retrograde handle also lands on the Pe marker and the vessel icon. The brief asks for an uncluttered gizmo.
findings.realReference: A translate gizmo seen down one of its axes shows that axis as a distinct toward/away glyph beside the pivot (or fans it out to a fixed screen offset); two axes are never drawn on the same screen line. KSP's node gizmo keeps the six handles visually separated at any camera angle.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/scene.ts lines 663-672: the handle's screen direction is the derivative of the perspective projection. For an axis along the view direction that derivative is (p.x, -p.y) / depth^2, i.e. the direction from the screen centre to the node, which with the planet centred is the radial direction. src/map/controller.ts line 485 then still draws it at HANDLE_MIN_FORESHORTEN (0.38) * 58 px = 22 px along that degenerate direction.
findings.fixDirection: When an axis' extent falls under about 0.4, stop using the projected direction: rotate it to a fixed screen offset perpendicular to the best in-plane axis (blend smoothly with extent so it does not pop), or draw the pair as toward/away glyphs at fixed offsets. Enforce a minimum angular separation (about 25 degrees) between any two axis directions and add a unit test over view directions asserting handle centres are at least one handle diameter apart and no handle lies on another axis' bar.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\accept-node-added.png (tooltip x 485-560, y 498-596 under the panel at x 558-790); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\hover-impact-details.png (tooltip x 669-982, y 380-464)
findings.defect: The hover tooltip collides with everything around it. (a) Right after the most basic action (click the orbit to add a node, pointer still on the node) the canvas tooltip 'Maneuver node / Prograde / Normal / Radial / Total / In' is cut off by the DOM panel that sits above the canvas: it reads 'Maneuver n', 'Prograde 0.', and the rest of its text ghosts through the 94 % opaque panel behind the panel's own rows. The same tooltip covers the prograde handle of the gizmo that was just created. It also only repeats what the panel shows. With panel offset (+92, +28) and tooltip offset (+18, +18) this overlap is deterministic for every hover of a selected node. (b) In hover-impact-details.png the tooltip slices through two labels: 'T-3d 19h 26' loses its last character and the lower half of 'T-3d 14h 56m' is covered by the tooltip's top edge.
findings.realReference: Shipped UIs never let a tooltip intersect a modal panel or clip neighbouring text: the tooltip flips to a free quadrant, and labels under it are hidden whole, not cut through glyphs. No tooltip is shown for an object whose inspector panel is already open.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/controller.ts lines 875-890: the tooltip is placed at hoverPos + 18 px and flipped only at the viewport edges; it is not part of declutter(), ignores this.blocked (the panel rectangle, lines 857-866) and the handle positions; tooltipLines() (lines 914-927) returns the node tooltip even when the node is selected. Labels are emitted before and independently of the tooltip rectangle.
findings.fixDirection: Do not show the node/handle tooltip for the selected node (the panel is its tooltip; keep at most the one-line drag hint). Choose the tooltip quadrant that intersects neither the panel rectangle nor any handle of the selected gizmo, then pass the tooltip rectangle to declutter() as a blocked rectangle (or hide intersecting labels whole). Consider placing the panel on the side of the node away from the body centre so it does not cover the trajectory just downstream of the node. Add a browser check: bounding boxes of tooltip, panel and handles are pairwise disjoint after adding a node.

findings.defect: Labels are struck through by the lines they describe. The vessel's own trajectory runs through the words 'Fake vessel' and 'Pe 100.0 km'; the cyan orbit crosses the Ap label's time line; the dashed planned patch runs between 'W' and 'miss' of the impact label; the Moon's SOI circle and orbit line cut through the Pe label; trajectory and dashed lines cross 'Node 1'. The 1.5 px dark halo does not separate text from a 2.5 px bright line.
findings.realReference: Map-view labels in shipped games either sit on an opaque/translucent plate that fully masks what is behind them, or are placed off the line on its outer normal with a short leader. Text is never crossed by a trajectory stroke.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/labels.ts declutter() (lines 162-256) tests candidates only against icons, earlier labels and blocked rectangles; polylines are not obstacles, and candidate 0 (right of the anchor, vertically centred) is taken whenever it is free, which for a vessel or apsis marker is usually along its own orbit. Labels have no backing (glyph halo only, src/map/gpu/glyphAtlas.ts lineWidth 3).
findings.fixDirection: Either give every label a rounded backing plate (about 75 % black, drawn in the icon layer before the glyphs) so lines cannot show between glyphs, or add the screen segments of current/planned patches and body orbits (the sampled vertices are already in scene.verts) as obstacles with a cost, and order the eight candidates by the outward normal of the anchor's own line. Add a unit test: no placed label rectangle intersects a current/planned polyline segment when a free candidate exists.

findings.defect: Icons pile up and bury what they mark. At the Earth-Moon overview the Earth (about 9 px) is completely covered by Node 2's 16 px disc, the entry marker and debris ellipses, and it has no name label, so the home planet cannot be found. At the Moon the Pe ring, the impact icon (only a red arc is left visible), Node 1 and the Moon icon are stacked. In the 8-patch plan three node discs overlap and the labels 'Node 2', 'Node 3', 'Node 4' stand 20-40 px away with nothing tying them to a disc. Displaced labels ('Ap 425.9 Mm', 'Closest 162.6 Mm', 'Exit Moon') have no leader. The impact marker and its ground-point twin are drawn as two overlapping red crosses 9 px apart. At 1e9 m the Ap and Pe rings merge into a figure-eight over an invisible Earth.
findings.realReference: KSP / Orbiter / Elite orrery: a body keeps its name and stays visible at overview zoom; coincident markers collapse into one stacked badge that fans out on hover; a label that is moved away from its marker gets a leader line; a marker never hides the planet it orbits.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/constants.ts SMALL_OBJECT_PX = 6: a body gets an icon and label only under 6 px, so between 6 px and the size where it is recognisable it is an unlabelled speck (controller.ts lines 782-791). There is no clustering: every marker is drawn at MARKER_RADIUS_PX 6.5 / NODE_RADIUS_PX 8 at its exact point (controller.ts lines 808-843), the '/surface' twin is always added (scene.ts line 484), and labels carry no leader (lines 868-873).
findings.fixDirection: Label every body whose disc is under about 40 px (and always when an icon overlaps it). Skip the surface-point marker while it is within about 12 px of its parent marker. Cluster icons closer than about 10 px: draw the highest priority one plus a count badge, or fan them out radially with leader lines to the true point; draw a 1 px leader whenever a label is placed farther than its nearest candidate. Shrink unselected node discs (5 px) so a node at perigee does not cover a 9 px planet.

findings.view: all 25 screenshots in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\ (e.g. accept-recovery-zones.png, scene-lowOrbit.png, accept-zoom-200km.png)
findings.defect: Every screenshot shows the overlay above the lab-only backdrop: untextured Lambert spheres with a stair-stepped (un-antialiased) limb on black. There is no evidence of the map over the real renderer (no map screenshot in out/screens/integration, labs/integration does not create the map view). Already on this mid-grey sphere the surface-target labels are weak: 'Central Pacific' glyphs measure RGB 167,179,196 on a background of 114,124,138 (luminance ratio about 2.0:1), 'Ka Lae Pacific Spaceport, Launch Complex 1' about 1.5:1; they read only through the black halo and look muddy. Over a tonemapped Earth with white cloud and a bright atmosphere limb the dim text (#aab6c8 with alpha), the green zone circles and the light-blue apsis rings will lose more contrast, and the bare-radius occluder will leave lines visible through the atmosphere glow. (Screenshots are from 2026-11-10 22:18, newer than the last src/map commit at 17:17, so the specs were not re-run.)
findings.realReference: The shipped view is the overlay on the real Earth and Moon: text on a bright planet is white on a dark plate or has a wide soft shadow (contrast 4.5:1 or better), and lines end where the visible limb (including atmosphere) ends.
findings.likelyCause: labs/map-view/backdrop.ts is the only background the package was ever judged against; label colours COLORS.textDim (#aab6c8) times the target alpha in src/map/controller.ts lines 775-779, halo COLORS.halo 0.85 with a 1.5 px stroke; occluders use BodyDef.radius only (hand-off known limit).
findings.fixDirection: Add a screenshot spec that activates the map view in the integration lab over the real Earth (day side with cloud, limb, night side) and the real Moon, and tune there: full-white label text with a backing plate or a 3 px soft shadow on lit bodies, target labels at alpha 1 once shown, occluder radius extended by the atmosphere's visible height for bodies that have one. Until then treat legibility over lit bodies as unproven.

findings.defect: Lines that pass behind a body do not stop at the limb: they continue up to 6 px over the disc as a fading stub. Over the lit lunar limb the two Moon-orbit lines show as short bright ticks lying on the surface, which reads as the line being in front of the planet for a few pixels.
findings.realReference: An occluded line vanishes at the limb; one to two pixels of softness is enough to avoid a hard cut.
findings.likelyCause: The hidden weight ramps from 0 at the limb to 1 only OCCLUSION_FADE_PX = 6 px inside it (src/map/constants.ts line 26; src/map/occlusion.ts lines 48-50; shaders.ts lines 46-48).
findings.fixDirection: Reduce the ramp to about 1.5 px (or make it proportional to line width), keeping the smoothstep. If a visible cue for 'goes behind' is wanted, keep the hidden part at a low constant alpha outside the disc region instead of bleeding it over the disc.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\accept-recovery-zones.png (Central Pacific circle right side around 735-740, 320-400; South Pacific circle around 790-797, 440-470)
findings.defect: The recovery-zone circles are visibly polygonal: straight chords with corners can be picked out along the right-hand arcs (clear at 4x, noticeable at 1x as slight kinks). They are 2 px wide at 0.9 alpha, the most prominent strokes on the disc, yet are sampled with the tolerance meant for faint debris lines.
findings.realReference: A circle of this size on a globe is a smooth curve; chord error should be below about a third of a pixel, as for the trajectory patches.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/scene.ts line 725 classes 'recoveryZone' as faint, so sampleLine uses FAINT_CHORD_TOLERANCE_PX = 0.9 (constants.ts line 18), while addZoneLine draws it at FAINT_LINE_WIDTH_PX + 0.5 with COLORS.recovery alpha 0.9.
findings.fixDirection: Sample zone circles with CHORD_TOLERANCE_PX (they are at most a handful of lines). This also reduces the chord sag behind the limb breakup in the first finding.

findings.defect: The node panel is translucent: the dashed planned patch, the Moon's orbit line and the AN diamond (at about 900,573) show through it behind the 'UT' row and the buttons. Faint at normal brightness, but it puts moving line work behind numeric fields the player is typing into. Icons are also allowed to sit under the panel (hand-off known limit).
findings.realReference: An input panel is opaque, or uses a blurred backdrop; nothing sharp shows behind text fields.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/panel.ts line 16: `background: rgba(10, 15, 22, 0.94)`; the canvas overlay keeps drawing lines and icons under the panel rectangle.
findings.fixDirection: Make the background opaque (or add backdrop-filter: blur with alpha 1 fallback), and skip icons whose centre lies inside the blocked panel rectangle.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\map-view\synthetic-earth.png (dashed pairs at x 400-640, y 440-720); synthetic-chain.png and scene-synthetic.png (dashed lines between 530,545 and 640,360)
findings.defect: Far-future planned patches are drawn as short dashes (8 on / 6 off) faded to about a third alpha, which on black turns the orange and pink of the planned palette into muddy brown and mauve; where the outbound and return legs run 2-3 px apart their dash phases are unrelated and form a zipper pattern. Inferred from the code, not visible in a still: the dash phase is the cumulative SCREEN length from the patch start, so dashes slide along the path whenever the camera rotates or zooms and can jump when the start of the patch leaves the screen or the sampler changes its breakpoints (no moving-camera sequence with a dashed patch exists in the screenshot set).
findings.realReference: Planned-orbit dashes keep a recognisable hue at any fade, and stay put on the path under camera motion (phase tied to the curve parameter or anchored at the node), so the pattern does not crawl.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/scene.ts lines 745-752 (verts.len accumulates projected segment lengths), shaders.ts lines 183-189 (dash from that length), constants.ts DASH_PERIOD_PX 14 / DASH_ON_PX 8, FADE_FLOOR 0.32 applied as alpha (scene.ts line 910).
findings.fixDirection: Anchor the dash phase at the patch's node end and derive it from a view-stable parameter (e.g. screen length measured outward from the node's projected point, or arc parameter scaled by the local pixel scale), lengthen the dashes (12 on / 8 off), and fade planned patches toward a lighter tint of their own hue rather than toward black. Record a short orbit-camera sequence of a dashed patch and check that a dash near the node stays within a pixel.
